```
354	# Patterns that indicate the worker's *session history* has absorbed an
355	# obsolete environmental failure (e.g. from an earlier invocation before the
356	# container was configured for trusted-mode). On a later invocation the model
357	# reads this history, believes the environment is still broken, and returns

359	# Detecting these in the raw output and invalidating the session forces a

370	def _is_rollout_missing(raw: str) -> bool:
371	    """Detect Codex's signal that a session/thread id has no rollout.
372	
373	    Happens when: container was restarted between phases and codex's session
374	    store (usually ``$HOME/.codex/sessions``) was wiped, but megaplan's plan
375	    state still has the session id and tries to ``codex exec resume <id>``.
376	
377	    Match is case-insensitive on known substrings so minor wording changes
378	    upstream don't break recovery. Fall back to failing loudly if Codex
379	    introduces a new error string — false positives here would mask real
380	    session crashes.
381	    """
382	    if not raw:
383	        return False
384	    lowered = raw.lower()
385	    return any(pat in lowered for pat in _ROLLOUT_MISSING_PATTERNS)
386	
387	
388	def _is_poisoned_environmental_failure(raw: str) -> bool:
389	    """Detect obsolete sandbox/environment failure beliefs in worker output.
390	
391	    Returns True when the raw output contains known-stale environment errors
392	    that a persistent session may have absorbed from a prior invocation
393	    (before trusted-container mode was enabled). See the comment on
394	    ``_POISONED_SESSION_PATTERNS`` above for motivation.
395	
396	    The check is intentionally conservative: every pattern is a conjunction
397	    of substrings all of which must be present (case-insensitive). A single
398	    sandbox error combined with a generic "Permission denied" elsewhere in a
399	    long trace should not trigger unless the full phrase appears.
400	    """
401	    if not raw:
402	        return False
403	    lowered = raw.lower()
404	    for group in _POISONED_SESSION_PATTERNS:
405	        if all(sub in lowered for sub in group):
406	            return True
407	    return False
```

> AGENT

Found the root cause. The Codex config at `~/.codex/config.toml` has `default_permissions = "full-access"` which defines a custom permissions profile with only network rules — no filesystem entries. Codex 0.125.0 doesn't recognize the profile format, so it restricts all filesystem access, making every command fail with exit -1. The `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` flag bypasses the sandbox but NOT the internal permissions system.

I need to fix three things:
1. The Codex config (root cause of sprint failures)
2. The "all-skipped = success" quality gate bug in megaplan
3. The poisoned session detection for this error pattern

Let me fix all three in parallel.

All three sprints are running fresh Codex sessions with `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, no `full-access` error, no stale session resume. Here's a summary of what I did and what's happening:

**Root cause found and fixed:**
- `~/.codex/config.toml` had `default_permissions = "full-access"` which defined a custom permissions profile with only network rules but no filesystem entries. Codex 0.125.0 didn't recognize it, so it restricted all filesystem access — every shell command failed with exit -1.
- Removed the broken `default_permissions` and `[permissions.full-access.network]` section. The existing `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` already provides full access.

**Three megaplan bugs fixed:**
1. **`execute/core.py`** — All-skipped quality gate: now blocks execution when every task was skipped with none completed ("execution produced no work")
2. **`workers.py`** — Added `"permissions profile", "does not define any recognized filesystem entries"` to `_POISONED_SESSION_PATTERNS` so poisoned sessions with this error get invalidated
3. **`handlers/execute.py`** — Added `_is_blocked_retry()` check alongside `_is_rework_reexecution()` to force fresh sessions on blocked retries, not just review kickbacks

**Currently running:**
- Sprint 2b (PID 31928), Sprint 3 (PID 34745), Sprint 4 (PID 35593) — all re-executing with fresh sessions
- Monitor watching for state transitions

Sprints 5 and 6 are still in `initialized` state — I'll launch those once the re-runs complete.

> AGENT

Line 1521: `_codex_exec_mode_flags(step)` returns `[]` for execute steps in trusted container. So the resume command has NO approval/sandbox flags. But the comment on line 1516-1518 says "resumed sessions keep the workspace that was granted when the session was created" — implying the sandbox settings should persist. But clearly they don't.

The fix: add `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` to the resume path for trusted container execute steps.

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan/megaplan/workers.py",
  "old_string": "    if persistent and session.get(\"id\") and not fresh:\n        # codex exec resume does not support --output-schema; we rely on\n        # validate_payload() after parsing the output file instead. It also\n        # does not accept --add-dir; resumed sessions keep the workspace that\n        # was granted when the session was created.\n        command = [\"codex\", \"exec\", \"resume\"]\n        command.extend(_codex_exec_mode_flags(step))",
  "new_string": "    if persistent and session.get(\"id\") and not fresh:\n        # codex exec resume does not support --output-schema; we rely on\n        # validate_payload() after parsing the output file instead. It also\n        # does not accept --add-dir; resumed sessions keep the workspace that\n        # was granted when the session was created.\n        command = [\"codex\", \"exec\", \"resume\"]\n        if _trusted_container() and step in _EXECUTE_STEPS:\n            command.append(\"--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox\")\n        command.extend(_codex_exec_mode_flags(step))"
}
```
